segments: This article retains the historical scope of NixOS 25.05 issues and corrects configuration interfaces against current official modules. Before use, check the project’s pinned nixpkgs, Home Manager, and quadlet-nix revisions. No system was evaluated or activated for this article.
There are three approaches to managing Podman on NixOS, in increasing order of complexity:

Enabling Podman through the system module does not force rootful operation: ordinary users can run it rootlessly, and whether sudo is needed depends on the intended workflow. Membership in the podman group is not a prerequisite for rootless operation. When the system Docker-compatible socket is enabled, group access to it may grant root-level management capabilities, so do not add users casually.
Approach 2: rootless Podman with Home Manager (recommended)
2.1 Enable Podman at the system level first
quadlet-nix is a Nix Flake that maps Podman’s Quadlet functionality to declarative Nix syntax.
Result: quadlet-nix automatically generates the corresponding .container/.network/.volume Quadlet files, which are managed by systemd.
The virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.podman.user feature in NixOS 25.05 has a known issue (nixpkgs #410857):
The systemd service may report Failed with result 'protocol'
In some scenarios, the container still runs as root

This issue is a historical record for the 25.05 release and affected scenarios. It does not establish that all current rootless oci-containers setups fail. First compare the implementation in your pinned branch with the issue’s status. If user-level management is needed, assess Home Manager or quadlet-nix while retaining the existing setup and a recovery path.
Directory ownership can cause problems when rootless containers mount volumes:
Pure declarative Nix + full Quadlet functionality
Keep the compose file and use podman-compose

Enabling the system module, generating Home Manager configuration, building, activating, and observing actual container behavior are separate verification layers. The examples assume that the host already provides the prerequisites for user namespaces/newuidmap; standalone Home Manager cannot replace every system prerequisite. Check subUID/GID ranges for conflicts, and do not simply change ranges when migrating existing storage. Set linger only when services need to run before login. The current Home Manager Podman module can generate Quadlet resources, so do not treat “Home Manager” and “Quadlet” as permanently mutually exclusive architectures. Use the actual generated output to determine service names. Nothing above automatically ran switch or deployed containers.

The current upstream Home Manager autoUpdate service also runs image prune -f after updating. Before enabling it, inspect the ExecStart/ExecStartPost generated by your pinned version, the schedule, and your image-retention requirements.
